name: Asking Data Questions in Plain Language
title: Asking Data Questions in Plain Language
answer: Asking data questions in plain language covers the practice of putting a question to a dataset in ordinary words and getting back a computed answer, rather than writing SQL or a script by hand. It sits inside quantitative analysis and reproducible work because the value of the answer depends on the question being recorded, the data being fixed, and the result being repeatable by someone else. The scope runs from simple lookups and aggregations over a table to multi step questions that join several sources, and it stops short of open ended modelling where the question itself is the research. In practice it is the layer between a person who knows the data and a system that can query it.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Asking data questions in plain language covers the practice of putting a question to a dataset in ordinary words and getting back a computed answer, rather than writing SQL or a script by hand. It sits inside quantitative analysis and reproducible work because the value of the answer depends on the question being recorded, the data being fixed, and the result being repeatable by someone else. The scope runs from simple lookups and aggregations over a table to multi step questions that join several sources, and it stops short of open ended modelling where the question itself is the research. In practice it is the layer between a person who knows the data and a system that can query it.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The usual setup is a database or a data warehouse holding the tables, a semantic layer or schema description that tells the system what the columns mean, and a language model that turns the question into a query. Execution happens against the real store, so the answer is computed from the data rather than recalled from the model's training. Supporting pieces include a query engine, a cache for repeated questions, and a log that records the question, the generated query, and the result. Where the data is sensitive, the model may only see the schema and never the rows.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts by pinning down what the question means in terms of tables, columns, filters and time windows, since most wrong answers come from ambiguity rather than from bad code. The system drafts a query, runs it, and the analyst checks the result against a known figure or a hand calculation before trusting it. Good practice keeps the generated query visible and versioned alongside the question, so a later reader can see exactly what was asked and what was run. Iteration is normal: the first phrasing often needs tightening, and the corrected phrasing is worth keeping as a test case.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are silent errors, ambiguous questions that produce a confident but wrong number, and access to columns the asker should not see. Provenance matters because a plain language answer is only as good as the query behind it, so the generated query, the data snapshot, and the model version should all be retained. Permissions should be enforced at the data layer rather than by trusting the prompt, and results that feed decisions should be traceable to a specific run. This site links to original papers rather than to a search tool, and the same instinct applies here: keep the path back to the source visible.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward tighter coupling between the question, the schema and the test suite, so that a phrasing that once worked keeps working as tables change. Evaluation is maturing from spot checks to curated question sets with known answers, which makes regressions visible when a model or schema is updated. Expect more work on clarifying questions, where the system asks back instead of guessing, and on keeping the generated query readable enough for a reviewer to sign off. The unresolved part is trust: a fluent answer still needs a checkable query underneath it.
